Verify that LoRA changes inference\\n\\nLoRA adds a low-rank update, `ΔW = (alpha / rank) × B × A`, to a base projection. The two official example adapters we inspected have identical weights and zero B tensors. Their zero update is useful as a loading control, but cannot demonstrate nonzero adaptation. The model checkpoint uses quantization-aware training (QAT); the exact serving build matters alongside the adapter configuration. Adapter activation loaded the canonical name, then reset the same module through an alias without matching weights. The inspected competition wheel avoids that duplicate registration when fast prefill is disabled. The organizer reports that the fix landed in wheelhouse v23. Our result below is tied to its recorded wheel hash, rather than a claim that the present wheelhouse still has the defect. The strong adapter changes the output and removes the base-leading token from its first-token top 20; the resulting decrease is **at least 4.8921 nats**. This is an inference-effect diagnostic; the synthetic adapter is deliberately untrained and is never packaged as a candidate.*\\n\\nThe successful path uses the competition vLLM **0.19.1** wheel, transformers **5.13.1**, compressed-tensors **0.15.0.1**, torch **2.10.0**, adk-submission **0.2.11** and swegemma **0.2.7**, with 257 frozen compatible packages. Train on the prompt the server actually sees\\n\\nADK replays earlier thoughts in `reasoning_content`. In the inspected vLLM 0.19.1 path, `chat_utils` reads `reasoning` instead. The recorded server prompts therefore contain the issue, tools and tool-call history **without past thoughts**. A second detail also matters: vLLM wraps string content as text parts before applying the template. Together, these two changes reproduce **803/803 native** and **133/133 held-out Rich** prompt lengths; the old renderer reproduces **0/803**. Dropping thoughts alone also matches zero; content parts alone match 79 first turns.\\n\\nThis mechanism was already reported by KE WU in [discussion 744354](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent/discussion/744354).
